modules.scope: code 唯一约束的编译/落库，以及重复键失败在 Repository 与 API 层的可识别性与 HTTP 映射。
modules.limitations: 重复键的绕行成本来自框架未公开类型化错误；应用侧实现（app/server/providers/devices.ts）仅作现象证据，不据此给框架加减分。

requirements.need: 设备编号在数据库层唯一，并发或绕过预检查也不会写入重复。
requirements.responsibility: 框架把 unique 约束编译为物理约束并交由驱动执行；迁移负责创建。
requirements.recommendedUsage: collection.unique('code', {name}) 或字段 unique；用 defineMigration 的 up/down 建/删约束。
requirements.actualUsage: app 迁移用 collection.unique('code',{name:'uq_devices_code'})；B03 并发重复被真正拒绝。

requirements.need: 应用能识别“唯一键冲突”并映射为 409/稳定 reason，而无需解析驱动错误或二次查询。
requirements.responsibility: 框架应公开可判定的唯一冲突错误或提供唯一冲突的 RepositoryErrorCode。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 当前无公开判定入口：isUniqueConstraintViolation 是 database/internal 实现，RepositoryErrorCode/Status 均无唯一冲突项。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用在插入失败后再 exists 查询以区分冲突，形成“预检查 + 失败后复查”的绕行。

requirements.need: 输入校验失败以 400 + 字段级错误返回，并可按 reason 本地化。
requirements.responsibility: apiValidator/invalidApiInputError 生成 INVALID_INPUT 与 fieldViolations；recognizeApiError 统一映射 RepositoryError。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 路由用 apiValidator 校验，onError 用 apiErrorHandler 统一转换；前端按 reason 本地化。
requirements.actualUsage: B02 漏填名称时显示字段级中/英提示，device route 用 fieldViolations 指向 code。

requirementFit.reason: 唯一约束本身可靠落库并保证并发唯一；但“应用可判定唯一冲突”这一接入缺口需要应用绕行，故拉低需求满足度。

usability.reason: 约束声明与错误体 API 易用，但缺少类型化的唯一冲突错误，重复键处理需要两次查询与自定义领域错误。

findings.title: 语言运行时与本地化错误在框架内形成可组合闭环
findings.detail: I18nRuntime 提供单实例、命名空间分片、先加载后切换与回退链；服务端 AppI18nError 在序列化时翻译并经 ApiError 暴露稳定 reason；客户端 useAppLocale 一步完成切换/持久化/通知。应用据此直接实现 B01–B06。
findings.impact: Agent 无需自造 i18n 机制即可覆盖双语界面、刷新持久化与中英错误提示，降低重复实现与状态不一致的风险。
findings.suggestedChange: 保持该分层；可补一个“唯一冲突=>ALREADY_EXISTS”的端到端示例，但本项无需改动。

findings.title: i18n 指引/Skill 覆盖文件位置、动态键、服务端翻译与检查清单
findings.detail: SKILL 与前后端指引明确命名空间即包名、文案入 locale、用 useAppLocale 切换、服务端用 getRequestTranslator/AppI18nError，并给出 tsc/locales check/浏览器核对等检查。Agent 在本轮读取并遵循。

findings.suggestedChange: 可在切换章节补一句存储作用域（浏览器级 localStorage + 会话级服务端）及其跨账号含义。

findings.title: @nocobase/db 未公开可判定的唯一约束冲突错误
findings.detail: isUniqueConstraintViolation 已在 database/internal 实现并能跨驱动识别 23505/ER_DUP_ENTRY/SQLITE_CONSTRAINT 等，但未从包导出；RepositoryErrorCode 与 RepositoryErrorStatus 也没有唯一冲突 / ALREADY_EXISTS 项。因此应用无法用类型化错误区分重复键，只能捕获后二次查询（app/server/providers/devices.ts:186-193）。
findings.impact: 每个需要唯一约束的应用都要自行判断驱动错误或增加额外查询，易出现泄漏数据库错误、竞态处理不一致与额外往返；框架自带的 recognizeApiError 已能映射 ALREADY_EXISTS:409，缺的只是可达的错误类型。
findings.suggestedChange: 导出 isUniqueConstraintViolation，或新增 RepositoryErrorCode（如 ALREADY_EXISTS / UNIQUE_VIOLATION）并在 repository-error 映射中落到 409，使 recognizeApiError 可直接产出标准冲突响应。

diagnosis.trigger: 向带 unique 约束的集合插入重复键（并发插入或绕过应用预检查）。
diagnosis.expected: 框架抛出可类型判定的唯一冲突错误或提供对应 RepositoryErrorCode，recognizeApiError 映射为 409 并带稳定 reason。
diagnosis.actual: 判定函数仅存在于 database/internal 且未导出，RepositoryErrorCode/Status 无唯一冲突项，应用只能二次 exists 查询。
diagnosis.workaround: 应用先 exists 预检查，并在插入 catch 中再次 exists 判断竞态冲突后抛自定义领域错误。
diagnosis.acceptance: 重复键插入产生可类型判定的错误，应用无需额外查询即可映射为带稳定 reason 的 409 冲突响应。

feedbackReview.reason: 冻结包证据支持这条能力缺口：@nocobase/db 内部已有 isUniqueConstraintViolation（E26），但公开导出不含它（E27）；repository-input 的 RepositoryErrorCode/RepositoryErrorStatus 也没有唯一冲突/ALREADY_EXISTS 项（E28）。recognizeApiError 虽能把 ApiError 或状态非 INTERNAL 的 RepositoryError 映射为标准响应（E29/E30），create 路径却不产生该类型化错误，应用只能在 devices.ts 里先 exists 预检查、再在 catch 里二次 exists 兜底（E32），路由再手动映射 ALREADY_EXISTS（E33）。替代解释不适用：检测函数已覆盖 Postgres/MySQL/SQLite 多驱动（E26），缺口在公开错误类型而非某环境或驱动特例，也不是工厂产物。

checks.reason: @nocobase/db 公开导出清单没有 isUniqueConstraintViolation，也没有任何唯一冲突错误类型（E27）；repository-input 的 RepositoryErrorCode 是封闭联合、无 ALREADY_EXISTS/UNIQUE 项，RepositoryErrorStatus 只有 INVALID_ARGUMENT/PERMISSION_DENIED/NOT_FOUND/ABORTED/INTERNAL（E28）。api-error 侧确实冻结了 ALREADY_EXISTS:409，且 recognizeApiError 只识别 ApiError/HTTPException/非 INTERNAL 的 RepositoryError（E29/E30）。故框架承诺了 409 响应映射，却没有可达的唯一冲突错误类型，改进空间成立。

evidence.excerpt:
# Goal

Put user-facing text behind a translation key correctly the first time: in the right file, under the right namespace, and in a way that survives a language switch.

# Scope

- Wire locale files into a package that has none yet.
- Add a string to an application or a plugin and render it translated, in the browser or on the server.
- Throw an error that callers see in their own language, and translate mail or jobs for their recipient.
- Add a language to a package that already has locale files.
- Reword a plugin's copy from the application, without editing the plugin.
- Translate a menu or breadcrumb title.

# Non-Goals

- Do not build a language picker. `useAppLocale()` exists; `app-template-default` already renders one in `client/layouts/components/language-switcher.tsx`.
- Do not add i18n machinery to an application. The plugin is registered by default, the client runtime is built by `createAppI18nRuntime`, and the server's by `I18nProvider`.
- Do not configure the list of languages. It is whatever the application's own `locales/index.ts` declares; configuration names only the default, `i18n.defaultLocale` (overridden by `APP_DEFAULT_LOCALE`). The `@nocobase/app-plugin-i18n` README covers that, `useAppLocale()`, the endpoints, and `useSyncServerLocale()`, which the template shell already calls to keep the server's language in step with the browser's.

# The one rule that decides everything

**A namespace is a package name, and the namespace in scope follows the render tree.**

An application's pages get the application's namespace; a plugin's pages get that plugin's, because the host wraps each contribution using the `packageName` it already records. So a component in its own package's routes translates with no namespace at all.

The exception is what most mistakes come from: a component a plugin exports for the application to render is in the _application's_ scope, not its own. It has to name its namespace.

# Procedure

## Wiring locales into a package for the first time

A package has a `client/locales/` and a `server/locales/` tree, each with an `en-US.ts`, the other languages, and an `index.ts` mapping every language to a dynamic import:

```ts
// client/locales/index.ts, and server/locales/index.ts in the same shape
import type { LocaleLoaders } from '@nocobase/i18n';

const locales: LocaleLoaders = {
  'en-US': () => import('./en-US.js'),
  'zh-CN': () => import('./zh-CN.js'),
};

export default locales;
```

# Verification

```bash
pnpm typecheck                    # a key absent from the interface
pnpm nocobase locales check      # a language declared on only one side
pnpm test                         # if application text changed
```

Run these from the application. Inside this monorepo the equivalents are `pnpm --filter <package> typecheck` and `pnpm --filter <app> exec nocobase locales check`. The root `pnpm i18n:check` is a different check: it reads every `locales/` directory under `packages/` and reports keys missing from a locale, without comparing the languages each side declares.

Then switch language in the running application and confirm the new text follows. A string that does not change is still a literal somewhere.

# References

This Skill is copied into each application that installs the plugin, so the packages are named rather than linked by path — where they resolve to depends on whether you are in this repository or in a generated application.

- `@nocobase/i18n` README — namespaces, the fallback chain, server-side translation, error payloads
- `@nocobase/app-plugin-i18n` README — the switch itself, the default language, endpoints, `useAppLocale`, `useSyncServerLocale`, and the session-stored language shared across tabs

evidence.excerpt:
# Copy and translation

All text a user can see goes through a translation key: titles, buttons, column headers, placeholders, `aria-label`, toasts and validation messages all count. Text hard-coded in a component cannot be translated, and changing its wording means changing code.

For the wording itself (which verb a button uses, how to write empty states and errors, how to put record names in quotes), see section C of [`../ui-guidelines.md`](../ui-guidelines.md); this document covers only how to write the code.

## Where copy lives

| File                             | Purpose                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client/locales/system/en-US.ts` | The template's own English copy: the shell, the sign-in pages under `auth.*`, shared components and the homepage. Exports the type `SystemResource`  |
| `client/locales/system/zh-CN.ts` | The template's own Chinese copy; typed as `SystemResource`                                                                                           |
| `client/locales/en-US.ts`        | English: spreads `system/en-US.ts`, then adds the application's own groups; defines the structure of all the copy and exports the type `AppResource` |
| `client/locales/zh-CN.ts`        | Chinese: spreads `system/zh-CN.ts`, then adds the same groups; typed as `AppResource`, so its structure must match the English                       |
| `client/locales/index.ts`        | One dynamic `import()` per language, so the browser downloads only the language being shown                                                          |

Rules:

- Write the application's copy in `client/locales/en-US.ts` and `zh-CN.ts`, never in `client/locales/system/`. The system files belong to the template, and a template upgrade replaces them; keeping the two apart is what lets it do so without touching the application's copy.
- A group the application writes replaces the system group of the same name rather than merging with it. To add a key to a shared group such as `navigation` or `appearance`, spread the system group first: `navigation: { ...systemEnUS.navigation, projects: 'Projects' }`, and the same with `systemZhCN` in `zh-CN.ts`. Rewording a system key works the same way: write the key after the spread.
- Each new feature gets its own group (`projects: { … }`), which holds all of the feature's copy.
- Add menu titles to the existing `navigation` group (`navigation.projects`), and write `navigation: { title: 'navigation.projects' }` in the route (see [`page.md`](page.md)).
- Add the key to `en-US.ts` first, then add the same key to `zh-CN.ts`. A key missing from `zh-CN.ts` or extra in it (including a misspelled one) fails type checking.
- The sign-in pages' copy is the flat `auth.*` keys; the authentication blocks in `client/extensions/nocobase-auth-*/` take their text as props, so `client/pages/auth/` passes these translations in.
- **Keys passed to `t()` are not type-checked.** `t('projects.titel')` compiles, and the page shows `projects.titel` as is. `tests/logic/app-locale-coverage.test.ts` catches it; run it after every copy change (its limits are in ["Checks"](#checks)).
- The English built into a few shadcn/ui primitives, such as the visually hidden "Close" of `Sheet`, is translated too (guideline C1): pass the translation as a prop where the primitive takes one, and otherwise replace the literal in the primitive with a key. ["English built into primitives" in `shadcn.md`](shadcn.md#english-built-into-primitives) lists each case.

## Language switching

`@nocobase/app-plugin-i18n` handles choosing a language and saving the choice.

- The account menu already has a language switcher: `client/layouts/components/language-switcher.tsx`, a shadcn submenu with radio items, which must sit inside `DropdownMenuContent` to keep keyboard navigation and the selected state. It is hidden when there is only one language. Do not build another selector, and do not store a separate copy of the current language.
- Read the current language from the `locale` of `useLocale()`.
- Do not switch languages with the `setLocale` of `useLocale()`: it switches only the interface and does not save the choice. When you really need to switch somewhere else, use the plugin's `useAppLocale()` (`@nocobase/app-plugin-i18n/client`), which saves the choice.
- Switching loads all of the new language's copy first and then switches, so the page never shows half Chinese and half English; components re-render, with no page reload.
- The application shell (`client/layouts/app-layout.tsx`) calls `useSyncServerLocale()` at startup; keep this call when you change the shell.

## Checks

Limit these to the changed files and the parts they affect:

- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: reports keys missing from or extra in the Chinese locale. It does not check whether the keys used in `t()` exist.
- `pnpm exec vitest run tests/logic/app-locale-coverage.test.ts`: reports every literal key the code uses (`t('…')` calls, including ones Prettier wrapped, and route `title`s) that either locale lacks, and every dynamic family (``t(`…${x}`)`` or `t('….' + x)`) with no key under its prefix. It does not check each value of a family: a missing `projects.status.done` passes while `projects.status.active` exists, so write one entry per value and look at each in the browser. It skips files that translate in a plugin's namespace (`useTranslation('@nocobase/…')`); a key held in data and passed as `t(item.key)` is not seen, so check those in the browser.
- After adding or removing a language: `pnpm nocobase locales check` (see "Adding a language").
- Look at the page in the browser in each language: no leftover English or Chinese, no key names; also check `aria-label`, placeholders, toasts and validation messages.
- Switch the language without reloading and check that the page follows: column headers, options, validation messages and date formats all update.

evidence.excerpt:
## Server-side text

API error messages, notifications and mail need translation too. The server translates them from `server/locales/`: `en-US.ts` states the wording and exports `AppServerResource`, and every other server locale is annotated with that type, so a key missing from one is a compile error. The template's server locales start empty — the server text that exists belongs to plugins — so add keys when the application's own endpoints start producing text. Name them by the same rules as client keys.

- The server resolves a request's language from the session's stored choice, then `Accept-Language`, then `i18n.defaultLocale`.
- Outbound content follows its recipient: mail, notifications and background work translate into the recipient's language, not the language of whoever triggered the work. A background job has no request to inherit a language from — resolve the recipient's locale explicitly and load it before translating. The `nocobase-app-plugin-i18n` Skill shows how server code translates, inside a request with `getRequestTranslator`, as an `AppI18nError` that the router's `onError` turns into an `ApiError` with a `localizedMessage`, and outside one with `getFixedT(namespace, locale)`.
- The frontend does not display an endpoint's `message` as is; it maps the status and the error's `reason` to its own copy (see [calling endpoints](frontend/references/api.md)).

## Keeping the server in step with the browser

`@nocobase/app-plugin-i18n` owns the language selector, persistence, and the server locale endpoints. The application shell calls `useSyncServerLocale()` so server messages use the browser's language when the server supports it; keep that call when changing the shell. If the server does not have that locale, the browser still switches and the server uses English; the language control shows an informational notice about the fallback.

## Which languages the application offers

The application's own locale files are the list. `client/locales/index.ts` decides what the browser offers and `server/locales/index.ts` what the server does, so adding a language means adding its file and loader entry on the side that needs it — there is no configured list to keep in step.

To add a language to the server, add its file annotated with `AppServerResource` (for example `server/locales/ja-JP.ts`) and its loader entry in `server/locales/index.ts`; the client side is described in [frontend copy and translations](frontend/references/i18n.md).

A plugin's locale file supplies translations for those languages, never a new one. A plugin shipping `ja-JP` to an application that does not offer Japanese puts nothing in the picker. Prefer keeping the client and server lists aligned when server-produced text needs the language. A client-only language is also valid: the interface switches to it, `PUT /api/i18n/locale` records English for the server, and the language control explains the fallback with an informational notice.

It defaults to `en-US`, and `APP_DEFAULT_LOCALE` overrides it. A value the application does not translate is ignored on the client and falls back on every key on the server.

The browser resolves its startup language as: the visitor's saved choice in `localStorage` → `i18n.defaultLocale` → `en-US`. The browser's own `navigator.language` is deliberately not consulted — the language an application starts in is the product's decision, not the visitor's operating system's. A default is never written to storage as though the visitor had chosen it, so changing configuration still reaches anyone who has not picked a language. Refresh after changing it.

# agent-browser core

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP, no Playwright or Puppeteer dependency. Accessibility-tree snapshots with compact `@eN` refs let agents interact with pages in ~200-400 tokens instead of parsing raw HTML.

Most normal web tasks (navigate, read, click, fill, extract, screenshot) are covered here. Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser web pages — see [When to load another skill](#when-to-load-another-skill).

## The core loop

```bash
agent-browser open <url>        # 1. Open a page
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 2. See what's on it (interactive elements only)
agent-browser click @e3         # 3. Act on refs from the snapshot
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 4. Re-snapshot after any page change
```

Refs (`@e1`, `@e2`, ...) are assigned fresh on every snapshot. They become **stale the moment the page changes** — after clicks that navigate, form submits, dynamic re-renders, dialog opens. Always re-snapshot before your next ref interaction.

## Always use your own session

Before your first command, set a named session for the whole task:

```bash
export AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION="$(agent-browser session id --scope worktree --prefix task)"
```

The default (unnamed) session is a single shared browser: it is shared with every other agent on the machine and it persists across conversations, so working in it can hijack another agent's page mid-task or navigate away from something the human left open. Every example below assumes a named session is active. See [Run multiple browsers in parallel](#run-multiple-browsers-in-parallel) and `references/session-management.md`.

## Quickstart

```bash
# Install once
npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install

# Linux hosts can install required browser libraries too
agent-browser install --with-deps

# Take a screenshot of a page
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser screenshot home.png
agent-browser close

# Search, click a result, and capture it
agent-browser open https://duckduckgo.com
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # find the search box ref
agent-browser fill @e1 "agent-browser cli"
agent-browser press Enter
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # refs now reflect results
agent-browser click @e5                        # click a result
agent-browser screenshot result.png
```

The browser stays running across commands so these feel like a single session. By default, an inactive daemon saves configured restore state, closes its headless browser, and exits after one hour; the next command starts it again. Without `--restore` or another restore key, shutdown discards transient browser state and open tabs. Dashboard mouse, keyboard, and touch input count as activity. Headed browsers, Safari and iOS WebDriver sessions, and user-attached browsers are exempt from the default; provider-owned cloud browsers are not. Use `--idle-timeout <time>` or `AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` to tune the timeout, and use `0` to disable it. Still run `agent-browser close` (or `close --all`) when you're done.

## MCP integration

For tools that support Model Context Protocol servers, start the stdio server:

```bash
agent-browser mcp
agent-browser mcp --tools all
agent-browser mcp --tools core,network,react
```

Configure the MCP client to launch `agent-browser` with `["mcp"]`. The server defaults to MCP protocol 2025-11-25 and accepts older supported client protocol versions during initialization. The default tools profile is `core`, which keeps MCP context small for everyday browser automation. Use `--tools all` for the full typed CLI parity surface, or combine profiles with commas, such as `--tools core,network,react`. Profiles are `core`, `network`, `state`, `debug`, `tabs`, `react`, `mobile`, and `all`; the `debug` profile includes accessibility audits, plugin registry, and command.run tools. Each tool accepts typed arguments plus `extraArgs` for advanced CLI flags and exact CLI parity. The common `allowedDomains` array maps to `--allowed-domains` and activates the same WebRTC containment and launch-mode restrictions, while `idleTimeout` maps to `--idle-timeout`. Tool discovery is paginated and includes read-only/open-world annotations so modern MCP clients can load the large typed surface incrementally. Use the tool `session` argument or `AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION` to isolate browser sessions.

## eve agent integration

For eve agents, mount the `@agent-browser/eve` extension instead of hand-writing browser tools. It adds namespaced tools such as `browser__navigate`, `browser__snapshot`, `browser__click`, `browser__fill`, `browser__find`, and `browser__screenshot`, all backed by agent-browser running inside the eve sandbox. The sandbox bootstrap helpers (`installAgentBrowser`, `agentBrowserRevalidationKey`) ship with the same package under `@agent-browser/eve/sandbox`, so `agent/sandbox.ts` needs no extra dependency.

## Reading a page

```bash
agent-browser snapshot                    # full tree (verbose)
agent-browser snapshot -i                 # interactive elements only (preferred)
agent-browser snapshot -i -u              # include href urls on links
agent-browser snapshot -i -c              # compact (no empty structural nodes)
agent-browser snapshot -i -d 3            # cap depth at 3 levels
agent-browser snapshot -s "#main"         # scope to a CSS selector
agent-browser snapshot -i --json          # machine-readable output
```

Snapshot output looks like:

```
Page: Example - Log in
URL: https://example.com/login

@e1 [heading] "Log in"
@e2 [form]
  @e3 [input type="email"] placeholder="Email"
  @e4 [input type="password"] placeholder="Password"
  @e5 [button type="submit"] "Continue"
  @e6 [link] "Forgot password?"
```

For unstructured reading (no refs needed):

```bash
agent-browser read                         # read rendered active-tab DOM
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com/guide  # docs-friendly fetch, prefers markdown
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com/guide --filter auth  # one matching section
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com/guide --outline  # compact page headings
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com --llms index --filter auth  # compact llms.txt discovery
agent-browser get text @e1                # visible text of an element
agent-browser get html @e1                # innerHTML
agent-browser get attr @e1 href           # any attribute
agent-browser get value @e1               # input value
agent-browser get title                   # page title
agent-browser get url                     # current URL
agent-browser get count ".item"           # count matching elements
```

Use `read [url]` when you need to consume documentation or other text pages rather than interact with a rendered UI. Omit the URL to read the rendered DOM of the active tab in the current browser session, including browser auth state and client-side updates.
